candidate_evidence.quote: This study is testing adjuvant Anhydrous Enol-Oxaloacetate (AEO) in GBM, an orally active drug candidate which in animal studies has demonstrated decreased tumor growth rate and increased survival.
Oral supplementation with AEO along with the Standard of Care (Temozolomide)

candidate_flag.reason: Oxaloacetate is marketed as a dietary supplement; record calls AEO a drug candidate (registered as DRUG) but also 'oral supplementation'. Whether it is a pharmacological candidate or a non-licensed supplement (excluded type) needs adjudication.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: A Phase 2, Randomized, Open-Label Study of Anhydrous Enol-Oxaloacetate in Subjects With Newly Diagnosed Glioblastoma Multiforme

role_evidence.quote: Anhydrous Enol-Oxaloacetate added to the Standard of Care (surgery, radiation and chemotherapy with temozolomide).

agents.drug_class_hint: oxaloacetate (anhydrous enol form), metabolic agent; also sold as dietary supplement
agents.stated_antitumour_mechanism: modifies cancer metabolism, reversing the Warburg effect, reducing glycolysis and lactate production

flag.reason: Possible non-licensed supplement (excluded type) versus investigational drug candidate.

agents.drug_class_hint: alkylating agent, GBM standard of care

coder_notes: Control arm is registered as PLACEBO_COMPARATOR but described as standard of care (no placebo described). Secondary outcomes include seizures and fatigue, but the record states an antitumour hypothesis and survival primary outcomes, so AEO is a candidate. Moiety has no INN; name kept as written.
